claims.text: SC joint: a saddle synovial joint between the clavicle and sternum; the costoclavicular ligament is the main stabilizer.
claims.quote: SC joint (saddle synovial): Bones: clavicle & sternum Ligaments: costoclavicular (main stabiliz), interclavicular

claims.text: AC joint: a gliding joint and the main articulation suspending the arm (clavicle, coracoid process, acromion), held by the acromioclavicular and coracoclavicular (conoid and trapezoid) ligaments.
claims.quote: AC joint (gliding): Main articulation to suspend arm Bones: clavicle, coracoid process, acromion Ligaments: acromioclavicular, coracoclavicular (conoid & trapezoid)

claims.text: Rotator cuff (SITS): supraspinatus (abduction), infraspinatus and teres minor (external rotation), subscapularis (internal rotation).
claims.quote: Rotator cuff (“SITS”): Supraspinatus (abd) - Infraspinatus (ER) - Teres minor (ER) - Subscapularis (IR)

claims.text: Shoulder ligaments: impingement occurs under the coracoacromial ligament; the glenoid labrum deepens the socket; the transverse humeral ligament holds the long head of biceps in place.
claims.quote: Coracoacromial: impingement under glenoid labrum: deepens socket Transverse humeral: hold biceps long head in place
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Glenohumeral joint ligaments

claims.text: Elbow ligaments: the ulnar (medial) collateral resists valgus and the radial (lateral) collateral resists varus; the annular ligament encircles and stabilizes the radial head (nursemaid's elbow is radial head subluxation).
claims.quote: ulnar (medial) collateral: valgus - radial (late) collateral: varus annular lig: encircles/stabilizes radial head -nursemaid/radial subluxation

claims.text: Forearm muscle origins: the flexor group arises at the medial epicondyle and the extensor group at the lateral epicondyle.
claims.quote: flexor group (OG @medial epicondyle): Musc: flexor carpi radialis & ulnaris, palmaris longus, flexor digitorum superficialis/profundus extensor group (OG @lat epicondyle):

claims.text: Carrying angle: normally about 5–15° of valgus with the arm fully extended and supinated; a gunstock deformity can follow a malunited supracondylar fracture.
claims.quote: the norm angle b/n upper arm & forearm (fully extended + supinated) ≈ 5–15° valgus; gunstock: can follow malunited supracondylar frx

claims.text: Wrist: 8 carpal bones in 2 rows; the anatomical snuffbox is bordered by the EPL and APL/EPB tendons, with the scaphoid in its floor.
claims.quote: Wrist: 8 carpals, 2 rows Bones: radial/ulnar styloid, Lister’s tubercle; anatomical snuffbox — border: EPL + APL/EPB tendons, floor = scaphoid

claims.text: De Quervain's tendons: abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis, in the 1st dorsal compartment.
claims.quote: abd pollicis longus + extensor pollicis brevis (1st dorsal compartment — De Quervain’s tendons)

claims.text: Bursae: the subacromial (subdeltoid) bursa lies between the acromion/deltoid and the cuff and becomes inflamed in impingement and bursitis; also the subscapular bursa, and the olecranon bursa between the olecranon and skin (olecranon bursitis).
claims.quote: subacromial (subdeltoid): b/n acromion/deltoid & cuff -inflamed in impingement & bursitis subscapular Olecranon: b/n olecranon & skin → olecranon bursitis

claims.text: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C7): biceps and brachialis; lateral forearm sensation.
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Brachial plexus, 5 terminal branches

claims.text: Axillary nerve (C5–C6): deltoid and teres minor; lateral shoulder sensation (regimental badge area).
claims.quote: Axillary (C5–C6): deltoid & teres minor + lat shoulder sensation (“regimental badge”)
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Brachial plexus, 5 terminal branches

claims.text: Radial nerve (C5–T1): triceps and wrist and finger extensors; injury causes wrist drop.
claims.quote: Radial (C5–T1): triceps + wrist/finger extensors — injury → wrist drop
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Brachial plexus, 5 terminal branches

claims.text: Median nerve (C6–T1): most forearm flexors and the thenar muscles; compressed in the carpal tunnel.
claims.quote: Median (C6–T1): most forearm flexors + thenar musc — compressed in carpal tunnel
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Brachial plexus, 5 terminal branches

claims.text: Ulnar nerve (C8–T1): intrinsic hand muscles and flexor carpi ulnaris; compressed in the cubital tunnel.
claims.quote: Ulnar (C8–T1): intrinsic hand musc + flexor carpi ulnaris — compressed in cubital tunnel
claims.locator: Anatomy section, UE: Brachial plexus, 5 terminal branches
